question: What does disease incidence specifically measure in a population?

options.A: The number of new cases developing over a specified period
options.B: The proportion of people who die from a specific condition
options.C: The historical average of chronic illness over a decade
options.D: The total number of existing cases at a single point in time

explanation: Incidence counts only newly diagnosed or newly occurring cases during a defined timeframe. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h1)

question: Why is tracking disease incidence crucial for community health workers?

options.A: It determines the exact number of hospital beds required for chronic care
options.B: It calculates the total mortality rate of an entire region
options.C: It measures the total economic cost of long-term chronic illnesses
options.D: It helps evaluate how rapidly a health condition is spreading among people

explanation: By observing the rate at which new cases appear, healthcare personnel can gauge transmission speed and direct resources accordingly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h1)

question: Which epidemiological measure includes both old and existing cases of a disease?
explanation: Prevalence measures the total burden of a disease by counting all current cases, regardless of when they first appeared. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h2)

question: A chronic disease has declining numbers of new infections each year, yet the total number of people living with the condition remains high. What explains this scenario?

options.A: The disease has a very short duration and high mortality
options.B: Prevalence is high while incidence is dropping
options.C: No new cases are being diagnosed anywhere

explanation: If treatments keep patients alive longer, the total pool of existing cases stays large even if fewer people contract the illness annually. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h2)

question: What must be excluded from the denominator when calculating disease incidence?

options.A: Patients who recovered completely from the illness
options.C: Individuals who have already contracted the disease
options.D: Healthy infants born during the study period

explanation: The denominator must only include people at risk of developing the condition, meaning those who do not already have it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h3)

question: A rural clinic records 25 new cases of Lassa fever out of a susceptible population of 50,000 residents over one year. What is the incidence proportion per 1,000 population?
explanation: Dividing 25 by 50,000 gives 0.0005, which when multiplied by 1,000 yields 0.5 cases per 1,000 people. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h3)

question: What is another common name for incidence density?
explanation: Incidence density is calculated using person-time units in the denominator, making person-time rate an alternative term. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h4)

question: When is cumulative incidence most appropriate to use as a statistical measure?

options.A: When every member of a fixed population is tracked for the entire study period
options.B: When individuals are followed for varying, unpredictable lengths of time
options.C: When study participants migrate in and out of the community constantly
options.D: When calculating the total financial cost of a chronic healthcare program

explanation: Cumulative incidence requires a closed population where all individuals are observed across the same complete duration. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h4)

question: Which factor is classified as an environmental determinant of disease incidence?

options.B: Total number of existing chronic cases

explanation: Environmental determinants encompass external conditions like water quality, sanitation, and climate that impact disease transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h5)

question: Why do seasonal weather changes often trigger a spike in malaria incidence in tropical areas?

options.A: High temperatures destroy existing immunity in adults
options.B: Monsoons eliminate all preventative healthcare clinics
options.C: Rainfall creates more breeding sites for vector mosquitoes
options.D: Cold weather forces people to stay indoors in crowded rooms

explanation: Rain provides standing water where mosquitoes reproduce rapidly, directly increasing transmission rates and new infection numbers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring incidence data in public health surveillance?

options.A: To measure the exact percentage of people cured by traditional medicine
options.B: To calculate the total lifetime medical costs of hospitalized patients
options.C: To determine the retirement age of healthcare workers
options.D: To detect sudden increases or outbreaks of new infections

explanation: Tracking new cases allows surveillance officers to spot unusual spikes and declare outbreaks early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h6)

question: Which action is most appropriate when surveillance data shows an unexpected surge in disease incidence?

options.A: Discontinue all data collection until the following year
options.B: Mobilize rapid response teams to investigate and contain the spread
options.C: Wait for chronic prevalence rates to naturally balance out
options.D: Assume the reporting software has a minor technical error

explanation: A sudden surge in new cases demands immediate public health action to identify the source and halt further transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h6)

question: Which Nigerian national agency primarily relies on incidence data for disease outbreak management?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control

explanation: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control coordinates national surveillance and outbreak responses using real-time incidence tracking. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h7)

question: A primary health clinic in a rural community notices a sharp rise in new cholera cases during the rainy season. What is the most effective immediate nursing action based on this incidence trend?

options.A: Transfer all pregnant women to tertiary urban hospitals
options.B: Focus exclusively on treating patients with chronic hypertension
options.C: Conduct community health education on water sanitation and hygiene
options.D: Wait for the rainy season to end without taking any action

explanation: Addressing the root cause of waterborne infection spikes through community education and hygiene promotion helps curb new cases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h7)
